gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured idle power for any of the candidates. ComputerBase measured the UGREEN DXP2800 at 18.6 W idle with two HDDs and 7.3 W with the HDDs in standby, and the same lab measured the J4125 Synology DS224+ at 18.6 W idle and 3.5 W in standby. PC-WELT measured the QNAP TS-264-8G at 26.5 W idle. ServeTheHome measured the GL.iNet Flint 2 at 5.6 W idle, and CNX Software measured it at 834–889 Mbps as a WireGuard server. For an always-on DNS + VPN box that is a 3–5× gap in power draw.
standout_why: I compared racksandwatts.com/guides/best-nas-for-a-homelab-2026 and racksandwatts.com/comparisons/ugreen-dxp2800-vs-synology-ds225-plus, which have only maker specs, no power, noise or VPN measurements, and never mention Pi-hole, AdGuard or WireGuard. comparefoundry.com's DS225+ vs DXP2800 page says it is based on maker documentation and has no measured figures. Synology's Container Manager page is the one ChatGPT cited, and it has no measurements. starryhope.com/nas/best-budget-nas (rank 14) gives one figure, OCinside's 'about 7 W at idle' for the DXP2800. It has no Synology, QNAP or router figures and no WireGuard throughput, and it does not say that DNS/VPN containers on the HDD volume keep the drives from sleeping. Our own page has UGREEN's lab figures and OCinside's, and lists 'not read' for the DS225+, TS-264 and Flint 2 idle draw.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's own caveat that a router or Pi beats a NAS if the shopper needs only DNS + VPN, and it puts numbers on it. In ServeTheHome's test the Flint 2 idles at 5.6 W, about 49 kWh a year (5.6 W × 8,760 h). CNX Software measured it at 834–889 Mbps in WireGuard server mode. Jeff Geerling measured a Pi 5 8GB at 3.2 W, about 28 kWh a year. A DXP2800 whose HDDs keep spinning idles at 18.6 W in ComputerBase's test, about 163 kWh a year. For a shopper who also wants storage, the DXP2800 remains the NAS pick: ComputerBase measured it level with the Synology DS224+ at 18.6 W idle, and PC-WELT measured the QNAP TS-264 at 26.5 W idle, so it doesn't cost more to run. One condition goes with that pick: put the AdGuard/Pi-hole and WireGuard container data on the NVMe slot, not the HDD volume. Otherwise the HDDs can't reach the 7.3 W standby state.

unsourced: Synology DS225+ idle power measured by a named reviewer on a page I opened. NASCompares' review (2025-08-04, Rob Andrews) repeats only Synology's 16.98 W access / 6.08 W hibernation and doesn't give a test setup. The Dong Knows Tech figure (275 Wh per 24 h) and NASCompares' '10 W idle' appear only on starryhope.com's aggregator page, and the Dong Knows Tech review URL returned 404.

TerraMaster F2-425 Plus measured idle power. ITPro's review (Dave Mitchell, 2026-02-23) showed only the 48 W adapter in the part I could read. Starry Hope's 12 W is a maker figure. CNX Software's Part 2 (2026-03-28) wasn't opened because I ran out of budget.
Asustor AS5402T measured idle power: not searched (budget).

WireGuard throughput measured on any NAS (N100 DXP2800, J4125 DS225+) by a named lab. The only N100 figure found was an anonymous blog (parkroyk.blogspot.com, about 636–658 Mbps) and an unverified OpenWrt forum claim of over 4 Gbps, so I left both out.
